1919, that tliis order will be strictly en-

The weekly report on the production
and shipments of bituminous coal and
shipments of anthracite coal, compiled by
the Geological Survey, Department of the
Interior, states that estimates place the
production of bituminous coal, during the
week ended February 8, at 8,040,000 net
tons which falls 291,000 net tons, or 3.5
per cent, below the production of the week
of February 1, and 2,521,000 net tons, or
24 per cent, below the corresponding week
of 1918. The average production per
working day during the current week is
estimated at 1,340,000 net tons, as com-
pared witli 1,860.000 net tons for the coal
year to date, and 1,744,000 net tons for a
similar period of last year.
The production for the coal year to
date, now estimated at 502,170,000 net
tons, exceeds the production of last year
for tlie same period by 31,129,000 net tons.
A continuation of the low production re-
corded during tlie past few weeks for the
balance of the coal year will cut tliis
excess down approximately one-half, aud
production for the coal year ended March
31, 1919, will not exceed 565,000,000 net
tons.

PROCEEDINGS OF THE CONGRESS BRIEFLY TOLD
SENATE.
Only a few minor amendments to the
rivers and harbors bill were considered
and agreed to yesterday. Much of the
day was occupied in the discussion of an
amendment for the improvement of a
stream in- Florida. Senator Jones, of
Washington, introduced a new female
suffrage constitutional amendment reso-
lution. He also introduced a bill de-
signed to punish those who urge resist-
ance to law or change in the form of gov-
ernmeut by force or violence. The bill
would impose a penalty of $5,000 fine
or five years’ imprisonment. In the
course of a brief speech. Senator Thomas,
Democrat, of Colorado, defended Mr.
Henry Ford against tlve cliarges made in
a recent speech by Senator Sherman, of
Illinois. Senator Chamberlain, chairman
of the Military Committee, made public
a letter received by him from Secretary
Baker, in which it was announced that it
was the purpose of the administration
to withdraw the American troops now
in northern Russia in the Spring. This
statement was based upon a message re-
ceived from Gen. Bliss, now in Paris, and
which was sent at the instance of the
President. The letter also stated that
the allied authorities had no fear for
the safety of the troops now in the vicin-
ity of Archangel. Senate and House con-
ferees reached a final agreement on the
annual post office appropriation bill. The
Senate conferees yielded on the amend-
ment continuing the pneumatic mail-tube
system, and the House accepted the
$200.000.0(X) appropriation for the con-
struction of roads. Other amendments
in conference were compromised.
The Judiciary Committee ordered a
favorable report on the nomination of
Thomas D. Warren to be United States
attorney for the Eastern District of North
Carolina. The Agricultural Committee
eliminated the item for free seeds from
the annual agricultural appropriation bill
and authorized an allowance of .$50,000
for an investigation of the cost of pro-
ducing staple farm products. Resuming
his testimony before the Propaganda In-
vestigating Committee, Roger E. Sim-
mons declared that if the allied Govern-
ments withdrew their forces from north-
ern Russia the Bolshevists would inaugu-
rate one of the bloodiest massacres in
all history. Before the Banking Com-
mittee Comptroller of the Currency, .John
Skelton Williams was heard in reply to
the charges that have been made against
his confirmation for another term.
HOUSE.
The House occupied itself yesterday
with the calendar and disposed of a large
number of uncontested measures, practi-
cally all of which were of minor impor-
tance. The Army appropriation bill was
laid aside, but was resumed to-day, when
a rule was brought in by the Committee
on Rules making in order the provision
for the organization of the Army for the
next fiscal year on a temporary basis of
500,000 men.
